guide.title: Haydn: String Quartet in D major, Op.64 No.5 – I. Allegro moderato
guide.overview: This movement is in two big parts, and each part is repeated. It is in D major and often visits A major, which is a nearby key. The opening tune is played by the second violin. Listen for the soft start, the loud passages, and the return of the opening tune in the second half. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so small details may be imprecise.

listening_points.headline: Second violin sings the main theme, softly
listening_points.text: The movement starts softly in D major. The second violin plays the main theme [m. 1-3]. The texture is a trio, which means three parts are playing together [m. 2-4].

listening_points.headline: The theme repeats, a little louder
listening_points.text: The volume rises suddenly to medium loud [m. 8]. The second violin plays the main theme again at the same pitch [m. 9-11]. The lines now move more independently.

listening_points.headline: First move to A major, led by the first violin
listening_points.text: The music moves to A major at [m. 11-14]. The key change gives a fresh colour. The first violin probably takes the tune, with the others accompanying [m. 12-16]. Then D major returns [m. 15].

listening_points.headline: Soft, then a build to loud
listening_points.text: The music drops suddenly to soft [m. 17]. A crescendo marking, meaning a gradual swell, appears at [m. 20]. Then it gets loud at [m. 22].

listening_points.headline: Loud passage in A major, then a bright E major
listening_points.text: The loud music settles in A major [m. 27-39]. The first violin probably leads most of this stretch [m. 31-42]. Sharp accents (sf) mark a brief move to E major [m. 40-41].

listening_points.headline: Soft, then a lone violin, then a quiet close
listening_points.text: The music turns soft at [m. 46]. Then it gets loud again at [m. 50]. The parts play the same line in unison or octaves, meaning the same notes at the same or different heights [m. 51]. The first violin is alone at [m. 52]. The part ends softly in A major [m. 56-59].

listening_points.headline: Part 2 begins softly, then visits G major
listening_points.text: Part 2 begins softly with a trio [m. 60]. The first violin then probably leads [m. 61-75]. It starts medium loud [m. 61], turns soft [m. 70], then loud [m. 73]. The key moves to G major [m. 68-74].

listening_points.headline: Minor keys darken the mood
listening_points.text: The music passes through B minor, then E major, then F# minor. These are loud, with the first violin leading [m. 79-86]. Minor keys usually sound darker.

listening_points.headline: Loud and soft jolts, then unison drive
listening_points.text: The volume flips between soft and loud in quick steps [m. 92-95]. Then the instruments play in octaves [m. 96-102]. The analysis marks measure 96 as the loudest point. It is only a computer estimate. The music then falls quiet [m. 102].

listening_points.headline: The opening tune returns in D major
listening_points.text: Home in D major returns [m. 103]. The second violin plays the main theme again at the same pitch as at the start [m. 105-107]. This time it is at medium loud.

listening_points.headline: Familiar music, now louder and busier
listening_points.text: A visit to A major [m. 109-110] echoes the first part. Then D major returns [m. 111]. The music goes soft [m. 113], then loud [m. 116]. The first violin probably leads, but it is often shared [m. 117-126].

listening_points.headline: A dip into D minor, then quiet A major
listening_points.text: The loud music moves through A major [m. 131-134]. The cello probably leads briefly into D minor [m. 135]. Minor keys sound darker. After that the music is back in A major [m. 138-147], with a sudden drop to soft [m. 142].

listening_points.headline: Soft return home, with a last detour to G major
listening_points.text: D major returns softly [m. 148]. Sharp accents (sf) mark a move to A major [m. 159-160]. Then a short visit to G major follows [m. 162-167]. The first violin probably leads.

listening_points.headline: Final loud flourish, then a quiet ending
listening_points.text: The music is back in D major for the end [m. 168]. It gets loud suddenly [m. 169]. The parts play the same line in unison or octaves [m. 170, 172], with a lone first violin between [m. 171]. The movement ends softly [m. 175-179].

glossary.explanation: The opening tune. Listen for it in the second violin.
The home note and scale that the music is built around. Changing key changes the mood.
Major usually sounds brighter. Minor usually sounds darker.
A sharp accent on a note.
Instruments playing the same notes at different heights, so they sound like one strong line.
One part has the tune and the others support it.
